text:
lee: Hey team — ACME just escalated an on‑prem private deployment streaming issue. Symptoms: SSE connection cuts out after ~25–45s, client sees partial chunks and then either a 0-length reconnect or no automatic resume. Happening only for their VPC/private nodes behind a corporate proxy + windows edge device. They say it used to be fine until they pushed an FW change last week. Trace id: trace:acme/0x9f2a

lee: Key details from the customer: model=rwd-medium, route=/v1/stream/chat, env=private, TLS terminated at corp proxy, keepalive used by client every 15s but still drops. They tried both our JS SDK and direct curl streaming.

nicole_acme: confirmation from customer — we see consistent partial events: the last event ends mid-line (no terminating 

), then connection resets. Their corp proxy is F5 BIG-IP with HTTP profile + TCP profile adjusted recently.

sara: Thanks, Lee. Any server logs? Are we seeing 499s or upstream resets?

lee: No 499s on our side. On the private control plane logs we see normal request start, then an abrupt connection close from upstream (private node) with no graceful SSE termination. Our runtime logs: "client_disconnect: remote_reset" and mib counters show bytes_sent stopped mid-event. No token/auth errors.

mike: Could be MTU/MSS fragmentation on the path — large SSE chunks crossing the MTU boundary and an intermediary rewriting or dropping packets. Windows proxies and some TLS middleboxes mishandle fragments. Did they report any MTU or MSS changes?

nicole_acme: They ran iperf and reported max MTU 1500 on VPC, but corporate edge does MSS clamp to 1400. They didn't change anything intentionally, but the team did roll out an updated edge ACL last Tuesday.

infra-bot: automated-check: nginx-ingress detected chunked responses proxied through corporate proxy; suggest proxy_buffering off and http2->http1.1 downgrade may be happening.

ben: Repro steps I tried from a staging onprem env behind an NGINX reverse proxy with proxy_buffering on. Repro was consistent: SSE payloads containing long event data (5–8KB) drop after a fragment boundary ~1400 bytes. If I toggle proxy_buffering off and set proxy_http_version 1.1 + chunked_transfer_encoding off, streaming stays alive. Example nginx snippet I used: 

```
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Connection "";
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_cache off;
proxy_request_buffering off;
```

ben: Also tried adding tiny heartbeat comments every 10s from the server (":" followed by newline) and that reduced client-observed disconnects in the nginx case.

paul: If the corp proxy terminates TLS and re-encodes to the backends, it may be aggregating or re-chunking. Some proxies will strip the Last-Event-ID header or collapse the trailing CRLF which breaks SSE resume. Nicole, can you confirm whether Last-Event-ID is preserved on reconnect?

nicole_acme: They said Last-Event-ID arrives sometimes but the header is dropped on the reconnect path frequently. When client reconnects with Last-Event-ID server-side resume fails because the resume token is associated with a short-lived connection id.

sara: Two parallel asks: (1) engineering: can we make our streaming resume less reliant on connection id and more on monotonic event seq so resumes succeed even if the proxy drops headers? (2) ops/support: get corp proxy team to test NGINX minimal config above or ensure proxy passes through chunked encoding and preserves Last-Event-ID.

deploy-bot: Deployment note: we pushed small change to runtime to add periodic SSE comment heartbeat (every 12s) behind a flag: flag=stream/heartbeat/enable. Rolling canary to 10% now.

mike: Additional low-level debug I requested from customer: tcpdump from inside their private node + tcpdump at corporate proxy (if allowed). Look for repeated retransmits around MSS boundary (~1400), and for TLS record reassembly. If we see many retransmits with identical seq numbers right at the 1400 boundary that's a smoking gun.

lee: Nicole posted attached tcpdump snippet (redacted) showing a pattern where packet with TLS record containing SSE chunk is split and an intermediate RST appears from proxy. They also pasted our streaming payload where the server sent event id and data then more data, but client got up to 1420 bytes then connection closed.

grace: Docs follow-up — we should add an SSE behind-proxy checklist to the support playbook: items to include: set proxy_http_version 1.1, disable response buffering, preserve Last-Event-ID header, ensure keepalive pings or SSE comments every 10–15s, MSS clamping check, and for Windows edge gateways verify no content-length injection.

sara: Short term mitigation options for ACME: (A) enable our heartbeat flag and ask them to roll out minimal NGINX passthrough config in their corporate proxy (if they can add a rule for Redwood domains), (B) switch streaming route to chunk size <1200 bytes by forcing server to break events (we can toggle server-side event chunking as an emergency), (C) fall back to long-polling (non-stream) route while they fix proxy.

nicole_acme: They accepted (A) and asked for (B) as a quick failover while corporate proxy team tests. Please share the server-side toggle and any expected side effects.

ben: Server toggle: we have a runtime flag stream/chunk/max_bytes override that forces event frames to be <= X. I set it to 1024 on staging and it stopped mid-event disconnects in our proxy tests. Side effects: slightly higher per-token overhead and higher request CPU. Recommend only for short windows.

paul: Long term: infra should add a resume path tolerant to missing Last-Event-ID by allowing resume via client-provided monotonic sequence or by server returning resumable sequence tokens in initial handshake. I'll open a RFC.

lee: Action items
- lee: coordinate ACME tests and get tcpdump from their corp proxy (in progress)
- paul: RFC for resilient resume (P0 for streams)
- ben: stage stream/chunk toggle and a runbook for enabling quickly for customers (ETA 4h)
- grace: add SSE proxy checklist to support docs (ETA EOD)
- sara: follow up on heartbeat canary and monitor error rate for the canary (watch for regressions)

sara: Thanks everyone. Nicole — please let us know results of the corp proxy rule test. If they can’t change their corporate device, we’ll enable chunk override and heartbeat for now. :thumbsup: 

nicole_acme: Will do. Appreciate the quick turnaround :heart:
